name: TypeScript
description: Senior TypeScript interview preparation aligned with TypeScript 7.0: narrowing, unions and intersections, unknown vs any, never, generics, keyof/typeof/indexed access, utility types, optionality, assertions and runtime validation, structural typing, mapped and conditional types, tuples, functions, strict compiler settings, and production type-safety trade-offs.

questions.question: What is the main difference between any and unknown?
options: unknown requires narrowing before most operations; any largely opts out of type checking
questions.answer: unknown requires narrowing before most operations; any largely opts out of type checking
questions.explanation: Both can receive arbitrary values, but unknown forces you to prove what the value is before using it unsafely.

questions.question: A value of type unknown can be assigned directly to a string variable without narrowing or assertion.
questions.explanation: unknown is not assignable to a more specific type until it has been narrowed or asserted.

questions.question: Which type represents values that should never occur?
questions.answer: never
questions.explanation: never represents an impossible value, such as the return type of a function that always throws or an exhaustively eliminated union.

questions.question: What is the practical difference between void and never as function return types?
options: void means the caller should not use a returned value; never means the function cannot complete normally
never means the function returns null
void means the function always throws
questions.answer: void means the caller should not use a returned value; never means the function cannot complete normally
questions.explanation: A void function can return normally; a never function cannot reach a normal return.

questions.question: With strictNullChecks enabled, which type accepts both a string and null?
questions.answer: string | null
questions.explanation: Under strict null checking, null and undefined are not implicitly assignable to ordinary value types.

questions.question: What does a union type A | B mean?
options: A value may conform to A or B
A value must contain every member of A and B
A and B are converted to any
questions.answer: A value may conform to A or B
questions.explanation: A union models alternatives. You may only use operations valid for the currently known member until narrowing occurs.

questions.question: What does an intersection type A & B generally mean for object types?
options: The value must satisfy both A and B
The value may satisfy either A or B
The compiler selects one at random
It produces an array containing A and B
questions.answer: The value must satisfy both A and B
questions.explanation: Intersections combine requirements from multiple types.

questions.question: Why are discriminated unions useful?
options: A shared literal property lets TypeScript narrow each variant reliably
They remove the need for runtime branching
questions.answer: A shared literal property lets TypeScript narrow each variant reliably
questions.explanation: A property such as kind or type with distinct literal values gives control-flow analysis a dependable discriminant.

questions.question: Given type Shape = {kind:'circle'; radius:number} | {kind:'square'; size:number}, what does checking shape.kind === 'circle' do?
options: Narrows shape to the circle variant inside that branch
Has no effect on the type
questions.answer: Narrows shape to the circle variant inside that branch
questions.explanation: TypeScript uses the literal discriminant to refine the union member in control flow.

questions.question: What is a common way to enforce exhaustive handling of a discriminated union?
options: Assign the remaining value to never in the default branch
Convert the union to an interface
questions.answer: Assign the remaining value to never in the default branch
questions.explanation: If a new union member is introduced and not handled, the value will no longer be assignable to never.

questions.question: What does typeof value === 'string' provide to TypeScript?
options: A runtime type guard that narrows value
questions.answer: A runtime type guard that narrows value
questions.explanation: TypeScript understands JavaScript runtime checks such as typeof and uses them for control-flow narrowing.

questions.question: Why does typeof value === 'object' not prove that value is a non-null object?
options: Because JavaScript reports typeof null as 'object'
Because objects have no runtime type
questions.answer: Because JavaScript reports typeof null as 'object'
questions.explanation: This JavaScript quirk means a null check is often needed in addition to typeof.

questions.question: What does value instanceof Error do in TypeScript?
options: Performs a runtime check and narrows value to Error in the matching branch
questions.answer: Performs a runtime check and narrows value to Error in the matching branch
questions.explanation: instanceof participates in control-flow narrowing when the constructor relationship is meaningful at runtime.

questions.question: What is a user-defined type predicate?
options: A function return type such as value is User that tells TypeScript how a runtime check narrows a value
questions.answer: A function return type such as value is User that tells TypeScript how a runtime check narrows a value
questions.explanation: Type predicates let reusable runtime checks inform the compiler's control-flow analysis.

questions.question: A type assertion like value as User validates at runtime that value actually has the User shape.
questions.explanation: Type assertions have no runtime validation effect; they only tell the compiler to trust the programmer.

questions.question: When data comes from JSON.parse, an HTTP response, or an external message, what is the safest general approach?
options: Treat it as unknown and perform runtime validation before trusting its shape
Assert it directly to the expected interface
Use keyof on the JSON string
questions.answer: Treat it as unknown and perform runtime validation before trusting its shape
questions.explanation: TypeScript types are erased at runtime, so external data needs real validation if correctness or security depends on its shape.

questions.question: What is structural typing in TypeScript?
options: Compatibility is primarily based on a value's shape rather than an explicitly declared nominal relationship
Every compatible type must extend the same class
Types are identified only by names
Interfaces are checked only at runtime
questions.answer: Compatibility is primarily based on a value's shape rather than an explicitly declared nominal relationship
questions.explanation: If a value has the required structure, it can often be assigned even if it was declared under a different type name.

questions.question: Two interfaces with different names but identical public structure are normally incompatible in TypeScript.
questions.explanation: TypeScript is structurally typed, so compatible shapes are generally assignable regardless of interface name.

questions.question: Why can private or protected class members make two otherwise structurally similar class types incompatible?
options: Those members must originate from a compatible class declaration lineage
Private fields are ignored by the type system
Protected members are converted to any
questions.answer: Those members must originate from a compatible class declaration lineage
questions.explanation: Private/protected members add a nominal-like compatibility restriction to class instances.

questions.question: What is a generic type parameter used for?
options: Express relationships between types while preserving specific type information
Disable type checking inside a function
Force all arguments to be the same primitive
questions.answer: Express relationships between types while preserving specific type information
questions.explanation: Generics let APIs remain reusable while carrying type relationships from inputs to outputs.

questions.question: What is the inferred return type of function identity<T>(value: T): T when called as identity('abc')?
questions.answer: string
questions.explanation: Type inference chooses a type compatible with the argument and propagates it through the generic return type.

questions.question: What does T extends { id: string } mean in a generic declaration?
options: T must be assignable to a type containing an id string property
T inherits runtime code from the object
T can only be exactly { id: string }
T becomes a union with { id: string }
questions.answer: T must be assignable to a type containing an id string property
questions.explanation: Generic constraints limit acceptable type arguments while still preserving additional specific properties.

questions.question: What does keyof User produce for type User = { id: string; name: string }?
questions.answer: 'id' | 'name'
questions.explanation: keyof produces a union of known property keys.

questions.question: Why is K extends keyof T useful in a generic property-access function?
options: It restricts K to valid property keys of T
It converts all keys to strings at runtime
questions.answer: It restricts K to valid property keys of T
questions.explanation: This lets TypeScript reject invalid property names and infer the corresponding value type.

questions.question: What does T[K] represent when K is a key of T?
options: The type of the property or properties selected by K
A mapped type over every key
questions.answer: The type of the property or properties selected by K
questions.explanation: Indexed access types retrieve property types from another type.

questions.question: What is the purpose of typeof in a type position, such as type Config = typeof config?
options: Derive a static type from the type of an existing value
questions.answer: Derive a static type from the type of an existing value
questions.explanation: TypeScript's type-position typeof lets types be derived from values without duplicating their structure.

questions.question: What does ReturnType<typeof fn> produce?
options: The runtime result of calling fn
questions.answer: The return type of fn
questions.explanation: ReturnType is a built-in conditional utility type that extracts a callable type's return value.

questions.question: What does Parameters<typeof fn> produce?
options: A tuple containing fn's parameter types
questions.answer: A tuple containing fn's parameter types
questions.explanation: Parameters extracts the parameter list of a callable type into a tuple.

questions.question: What does Partial<User> do?
options: Makes all properties of User optional
questions.answer: Makes all properties of User optional
questions.explanation: Partial is a mapped utility type over keyof User.

questions.question: What does Required<User> do?
questions.answer: Makes all properties required
questions.explanation: Required removes optional modifiers from the selected type's properties.

questions.question: What does Pick<User, 'id' | 'name'> do?
options: Creates a type containing only id and name from User
Removes id and name from User
questions.answer: Creates a type containing only id and name from User
questions.explanation: Pick selects a subset of keys from another type.

questions.question: What does Omit<User, 'password'> do?
options: Creates a type with User's properties except password
Sets password to never at runtime
Deletes password from an existing object
questions.answer: Creates a type with User's properties except password
questions.explanation: Omit is a compile-time transformation and does not remove properties from runtime objects.

questions.question: What does Record<Role, Permission[]> model when Role is a union of literal keys?
options: An object type with one property for each Role and Permission[] values
questions.answer: An object type with one property for each Role and Permission[] values
questions.explanation: Record constructs an object shape from a key type and a value type.

questions.question: What does Readonly<User> guarantee?
options: Properties cannot be assigned through that Readonly type
The runtime object is deeply frozen
The object cannot be garbage collected
questions.answer: Properties cannot be assigned through that Readonly type
questions.explanation: Readonly is a compile-time shallow restriction; it does not call Object.freeze or recursively freeze nested objects.

questions.question: TypeScript's built-in Readonly<T> is deeply recursive by default.
questions.explanation: Readonly only marks the immediate properties of T as readonly.

questions.question: What does the satisfies operator primarily do?
options: Checks that an expression is assignable to a target type while preserving the expression's more specific inferred type
Casts an expression to the target type
questions.answer: Checks that an expression is assignable to a target type while preserving the expression's more specific inferred type
questions.explanation: satisfies validates compatibility without replacing the expression's inferred type as a normal annotation often would.

questions.question: What does 'as const' do to a literal expression?
options: Prevents literal widening and makes object properties readonly and arrays readonly tuples
Marks every nested object method pure
questions.answer: Prevents literal widening and makes object properties readonly and arrays readonly tuples
questions.explanation: const assertions affect TypeScript's inferred types; they do not freeze runtime objects.

questions.question: const declaration and 'as const' have exactly the same type effect on object property values.
questions.explanation: A const variable prevents rebinding, but an object literal's property values may still widen; 'as const' suppresses that widening and marks properties readonly.

questions.question: What is the difference between an optional property x?: string and x: string | undefined?
options: The optional property may be absent; the required property must exist but may hold undefined
The optional property can never contain undefined
The required property may be absent
questions.answer: The optional property may be absent; the required property must exist but may hold undefined
questions.explanation: Object presence and the value undefined are distinct concepts, especially under exactOptionalPropertyTypes.

questions.question: What does exactOptionalPropertyTypes strengthen?
options: It distinguishes a missing optional property from explicitly assigning undefined unless undefined is part of the property's type
questions.answer: It distinguishes a missing optional property from explicitly assigning undefined unless undefined is part of the property's type
questions.explanation: This flag models optional-property presence more precisely.

questions.question: What does noUncheckedIndexedAccess do for undeclared keys covered by an index signature?
options: Adds undefined to the resulting indexed-access type
Throws at runtime when a key is missing
questions.answer: Adds undefined to the resulting indexed-access type
questions.explanation: The flag forces callers to account for the possibility that an indexed key is absent.

questions.question: What does the top-level strict compiler option do?
options: Enables a family of stricter type-checking options
Turns TypeScript into a nominal type system
questions.answer: Enables a family of stricter type-checking options
questions.explanation: strict enables stricter checks such as strictNullChecks, noImplicitAny, strictFunctionTypes, and related options.

questions.question: With useUnknownInCatchVariables enabled, what should you assume about catch (err)?
options: err is unknown and should be narrowed before accessing properties like message
questions.answer: err is unknown and should be narrowed before accessing properties like message
questions.explanation: JavaScript can throw arbitrary values, so unknown forces safer error handling.

questions.question: What is a mapped type?
options: A type that iterates over a union of property keys to produce another object type
questions.answer: A type that iterates over a union of property keys to produce another object type
questions.explanation: Mapped types commonly use [K in keyof T] to transform an existing object type.

questions.question: What does the -? modifier do in a mapped type property?
questions.answer: Removes the optional modifier
questions.explanation: Mapped type modifiers can add or remove optionality and readonly status.

questions.question: What is a conditional type?
options: A type expression of the form T extends U ? X : Y
A mapped type that can only return boolean
questions.answer: A type expression of the form T extends U ? X : Y
questions.explanation: Conditional types choose one type or another based on assignability relationships.

questions.question: What does infer do inside a conditional type?
options: Introduces a type variable inferred from a matched type pattern
questions.answer: Introduces a type variable inferred from a matched type pattern
questions.explanation: infer is often used to extract pieces such as array element, Promise result, or function return types.

questions.question: What happens when a naked generic type parameter in a conditional type is given a union?
options: The conditional type is usually distributive over the union members
The union is converted to an intersection automatically
The conditional always selects the false branch
questions.answer: The conditional type is usually distributive over the union members
questions.explanation: Distributive conditional types apply the condition independently to each union constituent.

questions.question: What are template literal types useful for?
options: Building string literal types from other literal types and unions
questions.answer: Building string literal types from other literal types and unions
questions.explanation: They allow APIs to encode string naming patterns such as event names or property-derived keys.

questions.question: Which type best models an object whose arbitrary string keys all map to numbers?
questions.answer: { [key: string]: number }
questions.explanation: An index signature describes unknown property names with a known value type.

questions.question: What is the key difference between an interface and a type alias?
options: Interfaces support declaration merging; type aliases can directly name unions, primitives, tuples, and other arbitrary type expressions
Interfaces can model objects but type aliases cannot
Type aliases exist at runtime but interfaces do not
questions.answer: Interfaces support declaration merging; type aliases can directly name unions, primitives, tuples, and other arbitrary type expressions
questions.explanation: Both work well for many object shapes, but they have different capabilities and extension/merging behavior.

questions.question: Both interface declarations with the same name can merge in compatible contexts.
questions.explanation: Declaration merging is a distinguishing capability of interfaces.

questions.question: What is function overloading in TypeScript?
options: Providing multiple call signatures for one implementation
Declaring multiple JavaScript function bodies with the same name
Automatically dispatching on runtime argument types
Using a union instead of a function
questions.answer: Providing multiple call signatures for one implementation
questions.explanation: Overload signatures describe supported call shapes; a single implementation handles the runtime logic.

questions.question: When is a union parameter usually preferable to overloads?
options: When the function behaves the same way for each alternative and the return relationship does not require distinct signatures
Whenever there are more than two parameters
questions.answer: When the function behaves the same way for each alternative and the return relationship does not require distinct signatures
questions.explanation: Unions are often simpler when overloads would merely repeat equivalent call behavior.

questions.question: What does readonly on a property prevent?
options: Assignment through that typed property reference
All mutation of nested data at runtime
questions.answer: Assignment through that typed property reference
questions.explanation: readonly is a compile-time restriction and is shallow unless deeper types are also readonly.

questions.question: What is a tuple type such as [string, number]?
options: An array type with known element positions and corresponding types
A union of string and number
A Record with numeric keys only
questions.answer: An array type with known element positions and corresponding types
questions.explanation: Tuples model fixed or structured positional data more precisely than ordinary arrays.

questions.question: Why is enum sometimes avoided in library/domain modeling when literal unions can express the same states?
options: Literal unions often stay closer to plain JavaScript and can avoid extra emitted/runtime enum behavior
questions.answer: Literal unions often stay closer to plain JavaScript and can avoid extra emitted/runtime enum behavior
questions.explanation: This is a design trade-off rather than a rule; enums remain valid TypeScript.

questions.question: What is excess property checking most likely to catch?
options: Unexpected properties on a fresh object literal assigned or passed to a narrower object type
Every extra property on every structurally compatible variable
questions.answer: Unexpected properties on a fresh object literal assigned or passed to a narrower object type
questions.explanation: Fresh object literals receive extra checks that do not apply identically to every intermediate variable under structural typing.

questions.question: What is the principal change in TypeScript 7.0 compared with TypeScript 6.0?
options: The compiler and language service were ported to native Go for major performance improvements while preserving TypeScript semantics
questions.answer: The compiler and language service were ported to native Go for major performance improvements while preserving TypeScript semantics
questions.explanation: TypeScript 7.0's headline change is its native implementation and parallelism rather than a redesigned type system.

questions.question: Which practices generally improve TypeScript safety at application boundaries?
options: Prefer unknown over any for untrusted values
Use unchecked type assertions to silence all errors
answers: Prefer unknown over any for untrusted values
questions.explanation: TypeScript is erased at runtime. Strong compile-time settings plus runtime validation at untrusted boundaries provide better guarantees than assertions.
